Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (latency / deployment / procurement path)

Hi Samir / Claire —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align internally and make your evaluation efficient.

Recap (from our discovery):
- Primary use case: customer support triage + assisted agent workflows (short prompts, streaming responses).
- Initial traffic target: 200 concurrent users, median request size ~120 tokens, peaks up to ~600 QPS for embeddings + chat mix.
- Critical decision criteria: latency (p90), per-token cost, deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and SLA (uptime + latency SLO).

Questions we committed to clarify:
1) Concrete latency targets (p50/p90) for the customer-facing flows.
2) Whether you require a Dedicated or Private deployment for data isolation & compliance, or if hosted API is acceptable for initial POC.
3) Procurement & security steps: who is the economic buyer, and who owns legal/procurement/security reviews?

Proposed next steps: 
- Samir: confirm latency targets (p50/p90) and whether strict tail latency (p99) matters.
- Claire / Procurement: share procurement timeline and any standard contract terms (we can provide an initial SOW/term sheet).
- I will loop in Connor (sales engineering) for a short tech deep-dive and Lauren (security) for compliance questions.

Attachments: I attached a short template to capture latency targets — please fill and send back (finova_latency_targets.xlsx). I also attached a preliminary Dedicated pricing sheet so you have numbers upfront.

Proposed check-in: Wed 6/9 10:00am PT to review filled decision criteria and next actions. Let me know if that works.

Thanks —
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

1) Latency targets: for the customer-facing triage flow we’re targeting p50 <= 150ms and p90 <= 400ms for text generation (end-to-end from request to first token). p99 is less critical for the initial rollout but we want to understand tradeoffs.

2) Deployment mode: for the POC we prefer Hosted if it meets the latency targets and cost profile. However, the security team is likely to push for Dedicated for production because of data isolation requirements. So understanding Redwood Dedicated latency/cost profiles vs Hosted will be important.

3) Procurement/economic buyer: the economic buyer is our VP of Product (Nisha Patel). Legal & procurement reviews are typically handled by Procurement (procurement@finova.com) and Legal (cc'd when needed). Claire is coordinating the procurement timeline — Claire, the rough target for decision is end of Q3, but earlier if the POC looks good.

I filled the latency sheet and attached it. Let’s plan the tech deep-dive next week.

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (latency / deployment / procurement path)

Samir — great, thanks for the numbers and the filled sheet. A few quick notes based on what you provided:

- Hosted: we can typically meet p50~<100ms and p90~<300ms on our hosted API for the short generation flows you described, depending on model choice (we can size around 7B/13B families to keep costs down).
- Dedicated: Dedicated gives more predictable p90/p99 with reserved capacity; you'll see lower tail variance and better throughput at scale but it comes with monthly committed spend.
- For the POC I recommend starting on Hosted to iterate quickly; plan a migration to Dedicated for production cutover if procurement requires isolation. We can support a canary rollout and side-by-side routing.

Connor — can you join a 45-min tech deep-dive next week to discuss model family choices, batching expectations, and streaming behavior? Lauren — can you weigh in on the basic security checklist so Samir and Claire can see what the Dedicated/Private checklist looks like?

Proposed slots: Tue 6/8 10:00am PT or Wed 6/9 2:00pm PT. Samir / Claire — which works?

Thanks,
Marissa
